author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected afterwards. The correction is judged by the same rules as booking, changes that same visit rather than adding another, and returns to the owner's record when accepted.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when its form is opened to correct it, then the form carries that visit's current date and description.
Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are supplied, then that visit carries the new details.
Given an accepted correction, when it has been stored, then the pet gains no further visit — the pet's visit count is unchanged.
Given an accepted correction, when it has been stored, then the owner's record is shown.
Given a correction with a blank description, when it is submitted, then the correction is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again.
Given a correction dated today or earlier, when it is submitted, then the correction is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again.
Given an owner's record, when it is opened, then it offers no way to reach the correction form.
Given a correction, when it is stored, then the visit still belongs to the same pet.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit — NG-5 still declines it
A link to the correction form on the owner's record; the owner deferred the visible way in to a follow-up request
Moving a visit to a different pet
Correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner
notes: PRD Visits section carries REQ-VIS-003 with five edge cases; edge case 5 records the narrowest reading — a visit dated today or earlier is correctable only by moving it to a future date, since a correction is judged by the booking rules. Two open questions recorded: whether a past-dated visit needs correcting, and whether the form gets a visible way in. The narrowing is recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-31-non-goal-visit-correction.md; the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR's status now names it. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside this agent's write scope and still needs adding.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope, but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the pet create/edit pattern applied to visits. PetController already pairs a create route with an edit route on one controller, resolving the edited entity in a shared @ModelAttribute loader that takes a nullable id path variable (read at PetController.java:75-87, findPet; grep-and-read basis, no IDE oracle connected in this run). VisitController gains the same shape: loadPetWithVisit takes @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId and returns the existing Visit from the pet's graph when present, the new-and-added Visit when absent. Correction stays inside the owner aggregate: no VisitRepository exists, the visit is reached owner -> pet -> visits, and owners.save(owner) cascades the update. That satisfies system-design.md Contracts (Owner is the aggregate entry point; Pet and Visit persist only by cascade) and the feature-package/no-service-layer ADR unchanged. Product decision already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-31-non-goal-visit-correction.md; no new ADR is warranted because the mechanism is the existing edit pattern, not a trade-off.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController, both returning the view pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm
loadPetWithVisit becomes the loader for four routes: it must branch on a nullable visitId and must not call pet.addVisit on the correction path
the correction POST binds onto the live Visit instance already inside owner -> pet -> visits, then calls owners.save(owner); the cascade issues an UPDATE, never an INSERT
docs/system-design.md Contracts rows for Owner, OwnerRepository, Visit and VisitController now cite REQ-VIS-003 (written by this dispatch)
docs/adr/README.md index gained the 2026-08-31 non-goal row and the narrowed status on the 2026-08-08 row (written by this dispatch)

patterns.description: findPet: shared @ModelAttribute loader with @PathVariable(name=..., required=false); returns a new entity when the id is absent, the existing one from the owner graph when present. Copy this shape for loadPetWithVisit.
initUpdateForm / processUpdateForm: the GET returns the shared form view and does nothing else, because the loader has already populated the model. Mirror both handlers.

the non-future date rejection with message code typeMismatch.visitDate. The correction must apply the identical rule; extract it into one private helper during the TDD refactor step so booking and correction cannot drift.
setAllowedFields disallows id and *.id. Keep it: the corrected visit is chosen by path variable and resolved through the aggregate, never by a submitted identifier.

risks.risk: The shared @ModelAttribute loader creates a Visit and calls pet.addVisit(visit) before every handler in the controller. Left unbranched, every correction request adds a phantom visit that owners.save cascades into an INSERT, breaking the unchanged-visit-count criterion.
risks.mitigation: Branch on visitId first: when it is non-null, resolve the existing visit from pet.getVisits() and return it without touching the collection. The test theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceWithoutAddingAnother must assert the pet's visit count, not just the redirect.

risks.risk: A mismatched owner/pet/visit triple could reach another owner's record (IDOR). No authentication exists anywhere in the application (system-design.md Security Context), so path consistency is the only control.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by scanning pet.getVisits() for the id — never a global lookup, and no VisitRepository. A miss throws IllegalArgumentException, matching the owner-not-found and pet-not-found throws already in loadPetWithVisit. This also delivers the two non-goals about visits or pets that do not belong to the named parent.

risks.risk: A flash message for the correction would add a new hard-coded English literal to the controller, extending the existing REQ-LANG-002 breach that the create path's "Your visit has been booked" literal already represents.
risks.mitigation: Add no flash message on the correction path. No acceptance criterion asks for one. If a reviewer wants parity, the message must go through the bundles, and I18nPropertiesSyncTest then obliges a key in all eleven locales.

risks.risk: The template reuse needs no edit, but a well-meant label change would introduce a message key and fail I18nPropertiesSyncTest across the locale bundles.
risks.mitigation: Leave createOrUpdateVisitForm.html unchanged. The form posts to the current URL because it declares no th:action, and the heading already drops the "New" prefix for a persisted visit via th:if=${visit['new']}. Any label change must reuse an existing key.

risks.risk: The no-link criterion cannot be tested in VisitControllerTests, which is @WebMvcTest(VisitController.class) and never renders the owner detail page.
risks.mitigation: Put theOwnerRecordShouldOfferNoWayToTheVisitCorrectionForm in OwnerControllerTests, which already renders owners/ownerDetails.html and already imports MockMvcResultMatchers.* and hamcrest not. Assert the rendered content carries no visits/{id}/edit href, and leave ownerDetails.html untouched.

notes: Visit has no equals/hashCode override, so Pet.visits (a LinkedHashSet) uses identity semantics — mutating a member in place is safe and needs no defensive copy or re-add. spring.jpa.open-in-view is false, so the loaded Owner is detached and an in-memory mutation on the validation-failure path cannot flush; only the explicit save persists. Concurrent corrections are last-write-wins: no @Version exists anywhere in this codebase, and adding optimistic locking is out of this slice's scope. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. The harness skew reported by scripts/doctor.py check (project-data spec_version 0.1.0 vs manifest 0.2.0) is pre-existing and untouched here, as instructed.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: REQ-VIS-003's edge case 1 ('Correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, is refused') and its PRD Done-when line have no test. `VisitController.findVisit` is the mechanism that enforces this — its javadoc states the guard exists 'so a visit belonging to another pet or another owner can never be reached from a mismatched path,' i.e. it is the IDOR guard for this feature. Jacoco confirms the gap is real, not just a documentation oversight: `lambda$findVisit$1` (the orElseThrow supplier building the IllegalArgumentException) shows `missed="9" covered="0"` instructions and `missed="1" covered="0"` methods — the not-found/mismatched branch is never exercised by any test in the suite. Add a test that GETs (or POSTs) `/owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit` with a `visitId` not present among the pet's visits (simulating either a visit belonging to a different pet, or an outright bogus id) and asserts the resulting failure — at minimum that a 5xx/error response results and the pet's visit collection is unchanged, consistent with how the sibling 'owner not found' IllegalArgumentException path is handled elsewhere per system-design.md's error-handling notes (REQ-SYS-002: exception reaches the generic error page).

approved_aspects: theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceWithoutAddingAnother pins the in-place criterion correctly via a singleElement() assertion on id+date+description, not merely the redirect — this is the load-bearing assertion the feature depends on and it is done right

theOwnerRecordShouldOfferNoWayToTheVisitCorrectionForm lives in OwnerControllerTests (correctly outside the @WebMvcTest(VisitController.class) slice) and is anchored by a positive containsString("Max") assertion before the negative not(containsString(...)) check, so the negative cannot pass vacuously against an empty or broken page
Blank-description and non-future-date refusal tests both assert field-level errors, status 200, and the redisplayed view name together — matches system-design's validation-failure contract

Test data follows the three-tier naming convention: TEST_OWNER_ID/TEST_PET_ID/TEST_VISIT_ID and BOOKED_VISIT_DATE/BOOKED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION are meaningful, role-named constants with no bare mystery literals driving assertions
Four-phase structure (arrange/act/assert, blank-line separated, no phase comments) followed in all new tests; BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming used throughout the new methods
AssertJ used for the new value-object assertions (assertThat/singleElement/satisfies) rather than JUnit assertEquals, consistent with the brief's assertion policy

Mocking stays within policy: only MockitoBean OwnerRepository (an I/O boundary) and MockMvc are used; Owner/Pet/Visit are real domain objects constructed and mutated directly, no new internal mocking introduced

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The new correction routes add the application's only IDOR control — path consistency across owner/pet/visit — and no test pins it. VisitController.findVisit (VisitController.java:98-105) and the owner.getPet(petId) null check (VisitController.java:77-81) are the sole barrier stopping a mismatched triple from reaching another owner's record, because the application has no authentication anywhere (system-design.md Security Context). The five new tests all exercise the consistent triple (TEST_OWNER_ID/TEST_PET_ID/TEST_VISIT_ID); none drives a visitId absent from the pet's visits, and none drives a petId absent from the owner's pets against the new /edit routes. A future refactor that replaced the pet-scoped scan with a global lookup would pass the whole suite while opening cross-owner record access. Class sweep of the new surface found these two instances and no third: the correction GET and POST share one loader, and no other new control is introduced.
findings.fix: Add two tests to VisitControllerTests covering the new /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit routes: (1) a GET (or POST) with a visitId that is not among the pet's visits — assert the request does not resolve the form, and assert the pet's visits are unchanged; (2) a request with a petId not belonging to the named owner. Assert on the refusal both handlers already produce (IllegalArgumentException from loadPetWithVisit), e.g. via assertThatThrownBy on mockMvc.perform(...) or by asserting the resolved exception, matching how the suite asserts controller-level refusals elsewhere. Name them as specification, e.g. theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet and theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenThePetBelongsToAnotherOwner.

approved_aspects: IDOR is closed structurally, as designed: findVisit (VisitController.java:98-105) scans pet.getVisits() for the id and throws IllegalArgumentException on a miss — no global lookup, and grep confirms no VisitRepository and no findVisitById anywhere in src/. Owner.getPet(Integer) iterates only that owner's pets, so the owner->pet link is enforced by the same structural means before the visit is ever resolved. A mismatched owner/pet/visit triple therefore cannot reach another owner's record.

Mass-assignment defence intact: setAllowedFields still calls dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") (VisitController.java:53-56), matching OwnerController and PetController. The corrected visit is chosen by path variable, never by a submitted identifier, and "*.id" also covers nested ids on the bound Owner graph.

No new mutating persistence path beyond the aggregate: the correction binds onto the live Visit inside owner->pet->visits and calls owners.save(owner), so the write stays behind the single OwnerRepository write path the design names.

Output escaping unchanged and safe: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is untouched, renders the visit through Thymeleaf th:text / th:field with auto-escaping, and no th:utext was introduced. The user-supplied description never reaches an unescaped sink.
No secrets in the diff: a case-insensitive sweep for password/secret/token/api-key/credential/private-key across the full change set returned nothing.
Supply chain unaffected: scripts/changeset.sh --name-only shows no build.gradle or lockfile change — no dependency added, removed, or version-bumped, so no new CVE surface enters with this slice.
New error messages carry only numeric ids (owner, pet, visit), no PII and no secrets, and error.html renders ${message} through th:text with Spring Boot's default include-message=never.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The two new tests raise `lambda$findVisit$1` from missed=9/covered=0 to missed=0/covered=9 (verified directly against build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml) and drive loadPetWithVisit's `pet == null` branch, but they do not pin edge case 3 ('a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, is refused') as literally stated. Neither test constructs a real colliding entity: VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET (2) is never attached to any pet anywhere in the fixture, and PET_ID_OF_ANOTHER_OWNER (2) is never attached to any owner anywhere in the fixture -- both ids simply do not exist in the test's object graph. As written, both tests only prove 'requesting a nonexistent id is refused', a materially weaker guarantee than 'requesting an id that exists but belongs to someone else is refused'. Concretely: refactor findVisit to `owner.getPets().stream().flatMap(p -> p.getVisits().stream())...` (scoped to the owner but not the specific pet) instead of `pet.getVisits().stream()...` -- this is exactly the pet-scoped-to-global regression the fix was supposed to guard against -- and both new tests keep passing unchanged, because visit id 2 still resolves to 'not found anywhere' either way; no fixture visit with id 2 exists on a second pet to be wrongly matched. Same argument for the pet-scoping test: no pet with id 2 exists under any owner, so a broken owner-unscoped `Pet` lookup (e.g. resolving petId against a hypothetical global pet index instead of `owner.getPet(petId)`) would also still throw, and the test would not catch it. Per testing-principles.md Coverage ('judged by behavior exercised, not lines touched'), the instruction-coverage gain is real but does not by itself demonstrate the guard the edge case describes. Fix: give the fixture a second pet on the same owner carrying a visit with id VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET, and post to pet 1's edit route with that visit id, asserting refusal even though the visit genuinely exists (just on the wrong pet); similarly stub a second owner (`findById(SOME_OTHER_OWNER_ID)`) whose pet actually has id PET_ID_OF_ANOTHER_OWNER, and post under TEST_OWNER_ID with that petId, asserting refusal even though the pet genuinely exists (just under the wrong owner). That is the shape that fails when the pet- or owner-scoped scan is swapped for a broader lookup.
